How this book matches your exam. IB Physics (guide first assessed in 2025) has five themes: A Space, time and motion; B The particulate nature of matter; C Wave behaviour; D Fields; E Nuclear and quantum physics. It is assessed as follows:

  • SL: Paper 1 (1h30: Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data-based questions), 36%; Paper 2 (1h30), 44%;
  • HL: Paper 1 (2h), 36%; Paper 2 (2h30), 44%;
  • both levels: the scientific investigation (internal assessment), 20%.

This book covers A.1 Kinematics, A.2 Forces and momentum (forces and circular motion) and A.5 Galilean and special relativity (HL). g = 9.81 m s⁻² and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. All calculations were checked with Python. The mark allocations are our own guides, written in the style of IB markschemes.

Unit 1 of 10: Describing Motion: Scalars, Vectors and Graphs

Key ideas

  • Scalars and vectors:
  • scalars have magnitude only (distance, speed, time, mass);
  • vectors have magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration, force).
  • Definitions:
  • velocity = the rate of change of displacement;
  • acceleration = the rate of change of velocity.
  • Graphs:
  • displacement–time: the gradient is the velocity;
  • velocity–time: the gradient is the acceleration, and the area is the displacement;
  • acceleration–time: the area is the change in velocity.

Worked examples

Example 1: a car accelerates uniformly from 0 to 25 m s⁻¹ in 8.0 s. a = 3.1 m s⁻² (3.125), and the distance = area = ½ × 25 × 8 = 100 m.

Example 2: a runner goes 400 m around a track and back to the start. Displacement = 0, distance = 400 m.

Example 3: a horizontal line on a displacement–time graph means the object is at rest.

10-mark exam-style question

A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 25 m s⁻¹ in 8.0 s, then travels at a constant speed for 10 s.

(a) Sketch the velocity–time graph. [2]

(b) Calculate the acceleration. [2]

(c) Calculate the total distance travelled. [4]

(d) Calculate the average speed. [2]

Answers:

  • (a) A straight line from (0, 0) to (8, 25), then a horizontal line to (18, 25) (A2).
  • (b) a = 25 ÷ 8.0 ≈ 3.1 m s⁻² (M1 A1).
  • (c) ½ × 25 × 8 + 25 × 10 (M1 A1) = 100 + 250 = 350 m (M1 A1).
  • (d) 350 ÷ 18 ≈ 19 m s⁻¹ (M1 A1).

Common mistakes

  1. Mixing up distance and displacement.
  2. Using the gradient of a v–t graph for distance.
  3. Forgetting the units of acceleration (m s⁻²).
  4. Averaging the speeds instead of using total distance ÷ total time.
  5. Reading graph scales incorrectly.

Quick recall

  1. What does the gradient of a v–t graph give?
  2. What does the area under a v–t graph give?
  3. Is velocity a vector?
  4. What is the displacement after one lap?
  5. What does a horizontal s–t line mean?

Answers: 1) Acceleration. 2) Displacement. 3) Yes. 4) Zero. 5) The object is at rest.
